  • phones did not work properly

  • phone instructions were insufficient

Two fellows who were in cells with me during various phases of the processing portion of the evening [1am - 3pm] were given hand written instructions for how to use the phone. Not only did the hand-written instructions vary, neither was exactly accurate. These two did not speak english and eventually were able to use the phones but only due to inmate assistance.

  • In the initial holding/processing cells, 4 of the 7 I was processed through had no toilet paper and 5/7 had severe caca-poo-poo issues on the floors and with the drinking fountains [which were on top of the toilets]

The operations in the Cell Block [after 3PM] were much better. But there were serious problems there too.

  • Phones didn't work

We had 4 phones, 3 of them never worked and the 4th had a stuck button. [#]

Once in holding there is a secondary PIN # to use the phones. This Pin # did not work for me in 3 days in spite of a written and multiple verbal requests to rectify.

  • Equipment breakdowns

The air hydraulics for the cell doors didn't work. Door latches didn't work.

  • Passive Aggressive guards

I did hear once in the 3 days someone come by to "reset Pin #'s" since they didn't work for anyone. I was reading in my room and my cell door did not open. Conferring with a Deputy on the next shift, there was no reason the door was not open.

  • Poor Signage

Throughout the facility there are laser-printer transparencies taped to the outside of holding cell windows. This works well in the well-lit processing environment. In the Cell Block, the environments are on the outside with the management hub in the middle. The cell blocks are well lit and the management hub is dark.

All of the signs that are supposed to show you your rights and expectations are completely illegible. They are laser printed black on transparencies with a glare on the front because they are behind glass and a dark background. Some of the line items on mine were further illegible due to smears and misprinting. Your rights don't matter.

  • Toilet Paper

Warrants a second mention because one poor guy in the intake part had really bad gutstick. He ended up using one of his own socks to wipe himself. Later, he was suffering. We asked for toilet paper a dozen times and were only provided it [from a closet 12 feet away] after he suffered for a few hours.

  • The worst insult

When I got my Motorcycle back from Impound they had stolen the Triumph jacket I have had for close to 20 years and have never put down. They also stole a 10 day old LS2 Modular helmet.

  • My $50

I had a $50 bill and my ID in my wallet, that's it. They gave me a debit card that had fees, and then didn't explain it. [And I didn't force them to explain it because there were 30 of us dressed in the release tank who all wanted to get out]

  • Because Fuck You That's Why

They let us out, in downtown San Diego, just about 10 minutes too late to catch the last Trolley.
Who are you Protecting from Whom and at What Expense?

The Good:

The Arresting Officer and his partner were very professional and did not make any mistakes.

I gave the partner a ration of shit. When I asked if I was being arrested and was told yes, I told them to fuck off and that we were done talking. He tried to help secure my stuff in the motorcycle. I told him he couldn't secure shit, and was angry since he had watched me unlock the seat and retrieve the motorcycle title from underneath. He was asking me an irrelevant question and I told him to fuck off, then later in his car after having been strapped to a chair and my blood drawn from a 20-know-nothing who whispered in me ear condescendingly 'make better choices' - I called him loudly and repeatedly stupid.

He was a good guy, so if I have any regrets, it's being so mean to him.

The Sheriff who learned that his eyes are too close together, however, earned my derision.

The phones were trying to sell me a service plan, and I didn't know how the system worked, so I was vehement in getting clarification regarding my situation. I have two dogs, and they were locked in the backyard with only one bowl of water between them. I wanted to make a call to make sure they would be taken care of.

He smiled at me and started to answer sarcastically. I told him "Don't be smart, because you're not".

It was like I threw Chi through the glass at him. He whimpered off. The man who replaced him, came over and politely answered my question - was a relief.

Soon after I learned that I could literally purchase 2 days of freedom from a bail bondsman for $250. My bail was $2500, but since I hadn't brought my credit card [my way of not drinking too much when I go out dancing] I would have had to pay 10%.

I told them to fuck off and put me in a Cell. The Point Loma Lt. Stood in their lobby like a grazed deer who was still hungry.

More Good:

  • The Mattresses are Awesome. I want one. Rolls up, lightweight, good heat retention.

http://www.chestnutridgefoam.com/correctional-industries.html

  • The cheap orange chinese sandals are ergonomic

I was wearing some flat motorcycle/dancing shoes [yes us sophisticates have such things] and my back did not hurt for 3 days until we got dressed for release.

  • Watching Football with guys who really cared about it

That was cool. Germany got kicked out or Germany won or something. I knew for a few days the details. The bottom line is they seemed to think it benefitted Mexico, and it was a really good hour or so watching the game with them. I remember a similar feeling in Bordeaux when France won some Ligue Championship. But the way they celebrated over there in Bordeaux - San Diego PD would have arrested the entire city.

  • Sock Man

One of the guys in post-processing had little holes for eyes and a mouth. The mouth was behind a rectangle in the translucent orange chinese sandal - and it made a funny face. Given more time I would have asked if the inmate made the holes or just appreciated the holes enough to orient them properly. Along these lines but not another bullet point - there were a few people who acted crazy to feel safe. The real bad ones, the ones who play in dark corners, they see this and prey on it.

  • One Final Thought:

In the release tank there was a guy who attacked another guy. He got an apology and 'control' without hurting the guy, but he already had his hands on him. Under any other circumstance I would have picked the little shit up and broken his will against a wall in one deft movement. But you can't fight, and I wanted to get home to my Dogs.

15 minutes later the deputies gave the assailant an opportunity to talk shit and he was thereafter moved to a separate holding cell.

You Gotta Entertain Yourself:

One of the shifts likes to make you get out of bed and close your own cell door after breakfast. I'm sure there is a good reason for it, but we had a 3-bunk cell and for the first 2 days I was the only one who gave any kind of fuck or was conscious. The old guy didn't give a shit, he had long hair. When we were in an initial holding cell I saw that his hair had gotten caught up on a screw and I wanted to reach over and detach him but it would have literally been brushing away another man's hair. An hour later we were literal cellmates and my first dream that I remember that first night was him coming back into the cell with a shaved head. Maybe he was younger in the dream, I don't know. Maybe it was his future and he is fighting in cancer. He only said a few things to me the entire time - "stop standing by the window", I am keeping him awake, stop kicking the toilet [I didn't know the toilets had an intrinsic flush delay and looking at my own shit infuriated me. If the toilet was Officer Gonjales his knee would have been broken and his throat would have been bitten open. My cellmate also told me to let them close their own fucking door. The first time I got out of bed to close the door, I stood behind it and stood on my tip-toes, and told the Deputy that I was closing it with my dick. But it didn't latch. Another Officer came over and closed it. I assume they had to latch the mechanism from the outside.

The next day, in a less generous mood, I slammed the door shut. But it didn't latch. I slammed it again, but it didn't latch. I slammed it again, but it didn't latch. The guy told me to stop being such an asshole and close it slowly. It latched.

More Entertainment:

"Tick Tock. "

...

"Mitsubishi"

He moved somewhere else that same day.
